summary: Northbridge AI: Request percentage-based canary rollouts on Hosted routes + questions on guardrails and rollback semantics
description:
Issue summary:
Northbridge AI is requesting percentage-based canary rollouts for Redwood Hosted routes (baseline vs candidate model/version) and wants clarity on guardrails (latency/error/cost/quality) and rollback/pause semantics, especially for streaming.

Customer context:
- Workload: user-facing chat + internal classification. They want to upgrade their primary chat route from a pinned model version to a newer version and reduce risk of regressions.
- Compliance requirement: wants an audit trail of rollout changes (who changed traffic %, when, and what was changed).

Customer ask / questions:
1) Can Redwood Hosted support splitting traffic by percentage between baseline and candidate on the same route?
2) What guardrails are available (error rate, latency p95/p99, token cost deltas, quality checks)?
3) Can we pause or instantly roll back? What happens to in-flight streaming responses and retries?
4) Can we ensure “sticky” routing (same end-user stays on the same variant) to avoid mixed experiences?
5) What’s the timeline for availability and how can Northbridge get access (beta/GA)?

Impact:
- Medium: blocks safe rollout to newer model version; customer is currently holding back a planned launch.
- Risk: without canary tooling, they would either (a) switch 100% at once or (b) maintain duplicate routes + client-side routing.

Environment:
- Hosted API, prod us-east

Current workaround discussed:
- Maintain separate routes for baseline/candidate and do client-side percentage routing.
- Alternatively pin model version and do a manual cutover during low-traffic window.

Requested next steps:
- Confirm if/when Northbridge can join Hosted canary rollouts beta and any prerequisites.
- Provide written guidance on guardrails + rollback behavior (especially streaming).
comments:
2024-10-08 (Dev Patel, Support) — Acknowledged request and asked for: (a) target route(s) and current model/version, (b) whether streaming is used for the route, (c) required guardrails (must-have vs nice-to-have), and (d) whether they need sticky routing tied to end-user identity or request-level hash.

Provided interim guidance: today we can do client-side splitting across two Hosted routes, but we’re actively productizing a first-class Hosted canary rollout workflow (Console + policy/routing). Flagged that streaming/retry semantics are a key design point; promised follow-up after confirming current behavior with Routing/Platform teams.

2024-10-09 (Miguel Santos, Customer Success) — Spoke with Northbridge (customer champion: Platform Eng lead). They confirmed: streaming is enabled for the chat route; they want sticky routing at least per session (to avoid user seeing alternating behaviors). Guardrails they care about in order: (1) elevated 5xx/timeout rate, (2) latency p95, (3) token-cost increase, (4) “quality” is desired but they can start without automatic gating if rollback is easy.

Added note: they also asked for an audit trail they can export (SOC2 evidence) showing rollout changes.

2024-10-10 (Marissa Cole, Product) — Product update: Hosted canary rollout workflow is planned for GA with a Console-first flow and underlying policy/routing controls. The intended GA experience includes:
- Baseline vs candidate selection (model + version)
- Percentage-based traffic splitting with manual steps and optional timed progression
- Guardrails: error-rate and latency thresholds at minimum; cost delta guardrail planned; quality gates optional and may be phased
- Quick pause/rollback actions

Timeline (subject to final sequencing): internal dogfood first, then limited beta with select Hosted customers, then GA. Northbridge is a good candidate for limited beta given their streaming use case and compliance needs (audit history).

Requested Support/CS to confirm: (a) target launch window they need, (b) regions, (c) whether they require quality gating at beta entry or can accept monitoring-only + manual rollback.

2024-10-10 (Mina Haddad, Routing) — Routing notes for customer questions:
- Percentage split will be implemented as weighted variants on Hosted routes.
- Sticky routing: likely request-hash stickiness option (configurable) rather than mandatory for all customers. For streaming, the variant selection is pinned at request start; we will avoid cross-variant mixing within a single stream.
- Retry behavior: planned behavior is that retries reuse the same variant selection when possible (to prevent a single end-user interaction switching variants mid-session).

Caveat: exact stickiness key (request ID/session ID/user ID) depends on what the customer can provide. We should recommend a stable session identifier header if they need per-user/session consistency.

2024-10-11 (Sean Gallagher, SRE) — Rollback/pause expectations (for beta/GA):
- Pause/rollback will drive policy weights to 0% candidate and propagate across regions.
- We cannot forcibly terminate already-running streams; rollback affects new requests. For long-lived streams, customer should expect existing responses to complete on the originally selected variant.
- Monitoring: per-variant dashboards will compare baseline vs candidate error/latency; recommend alerting on delta thresholds and having a clear rollback trigger.

Added: we should be explicit that the system provides “fast rollback for new traffic,” not “instant revert for in-flight connections.”

2024-10-14 (Dev Patel, Support) — Sent customer a written summary (drafted with Product/Routing/SRE input):
1) Percentage-based Hosted canary rollouts are in-progress; Northbridge can be considered for limited beta.
2) Guardrails planned: latency + error-rate thresholds; cost deltas planned; quality gates optional/phase.
3) Rollback/pause affects new requests; in-flight streaming continues on selected variant; retries aim to stick to original variant selection.
4) Sticky routing: planned as an option (request-hash stickiness) and best-effort based on a stable session key header.
5) Audit trail: GA scope includes Console activity timeline/audit history and security audit logging events for create/update/pause/rollback.

Asked Northbridge to confirm:
- Target date they need (earliest acceptable beta)
- Whether they can send a stable session ID header for stickiness
- Which guardrails are mandatory to start

Set status to Waiting on Customer.

2024-10-15 (Paula Mendes, PM - policies/telemetry) — Internal note: if Northbridge enters beta, we should ensure telemetry setup includes per-variant error/latency and cost breakdown at route-level with cardinality safeguards. Also confirm whether they require exportable audit events (SIEM) vs Console-only history (ties to SUP-4104).
next_steps: Waiting on customer confirmation of beta timing needs + session identifier approach. If confirmed, CS to nominate Northbridge for limited beta cohort and coordinate enablement with Product/Platform (feature flag + entitlements).
internal_notes: Track alongside Hosted canary rollout workflow (GA). If customer escalates timeline risk, route to Marissa Cole + Connor O'Brien for release sequencing. If audit export is a blocker, link to SUP-4104 and involve Kevin Osei (Security/SIEM).
